raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fix Python DeepSeek V4.1 rendering when tool results reorder image placeholders or thinking mode drops historical developer content. Carry source image indices through the native encoder and apply the resulting order to both image data and UUIDs.

This follows the source-order approach of #56366, which fixed the Rust frontend only.

## Claims

- Out-of-order tool results keep their own images after sorting into tool-call order.
- Images belonging to dropped developer content no longer reach multimodal prompt expansion without a placeholder.

## Validation

The following results are from the tests run on **2026-10-09**, not a new rerun. The four production files tested then are unchanged at the current PR head.

Two regression cases, each exercised through sync and async rendering; the existing V4/V4.1 tokenizer suites are also included.

| CPU tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline source checkout + regression tests | 4 failed, 75 passed |
| Patched implementation | 79 passed |

Run in a CPU-only container against the source checkout, with model/processor metadata stubbed and real message parsing, image tracking and native encoding:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=/work/checks/tests/tokenizers_ -o addopts= \
  /work/checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py \
  /work/checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py -v
```

<details>
<summary>Actual CPU output: baseline failures and patched result</summary>

Verbatim excerpts from `regression-baseline.log`:

```text
FAILED ../checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_tool_images_follow_rendered_order[sync]
FAILED ../checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_tool_images_follow_rendered_order[async]
FAILED ../checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_dropped_developer_only_image_leaves_text_prompt[sync]
FAILED ../checks/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_dropped_developer_only_image_leaves_text_prompt[async]
================== 4 failed, 75 passed, 15 warnings in 15.77s ==================
```

From `regression-patched.log`:

```text
======================= 79 passed, 15 warnings in 15.66s =======================
```

</details>

Full pre-commit checks passed on all five changed files, including mypy and test CI tethering.

**GPU validation passed** on the real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint (`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`), using 8x H20-3e, TP=8, eager execution and temperature=0. The GPU runtime was vLLM 0.31.0 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 with this PR's four production files mounted unchanged; their SHA-256 hashes were verified against commit `f5622b6`. This was not a full build of main.

The same loaded model compared the original media handling (the base renderer without an image-order accumulator) and the patched V4.1 renderer, using generated 560x560 red and blue images:

| Full-model case | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordered tool results, baseline | `A=red, B=blue` |
| Reversed tool results, baseline | `A=blue, B=red` (wrong image assignment) |
| Reversed tool results, patched | `A=red, B=blue`; output token IDs match the ordered baseline |
| Dropped historical developer image, baseline | `AssertionError: Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]` |
| Dropped historical developer image, patched | Successful generation, final answer `OK` |

<details>
<summary>Actual full-model GPU output, including generated text and token IDs</summary>

The in-container validation command was `.venv/bin/python /work/gpu_validate.py`. These are verbatim result lines from `gpu.log`, not reconstructed from the summary table:

```text
torch 2.13.0+cu130 vllm 0.31.0 gpus 8
```

```text
GPU_RESULT {"case": "ordered_baseline", "text": "A=red, B=blue", "token_ids": [35, 31, 1157, 14, 406, 31, 27602, 1]}
GPU_RESULT {"case": "reversed_baseline", "text": "A=blue, B=red", "token_ids": [35, 31, 27602, 14, 406, 31, 1157, 1]}
GPU_RESULT {"case": "reversed_patched", "text": "A=red, B=blue", "token_ids": [35, 31, 1157, 14, 406, 31, 27602, 1]}
GPU_RESULT {"case": "developer_baseline", "error_type": "AssertionError", "error": "Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]"}
GPU_RESULT {"case": "developer_patched", "text": "We need answer user says \"Reply OK.\" So just reply OK. Need comply. final maybe \"OK\".</think>OK", "token_ids": [2581, 1309, 3287, 3967, 4230, 582, 19905, 20370, 2148, 3016, 1438, 20430, 20370, 16, 21017, 27233, 16, 4087, 10796, 582, 11932, 3305, 128822, 11932, 1]}
GPU_VALIDATION_PASSED
```

The log subsequently contains shutdown warnings about force-killing the remaining EngineCore and one leaked shared-memory object. The pass marker covers the inference assertions above, not a warning-free shutdown.

</details>

These checks verify the two rendering regressions, not performance or general model accuracy.

## Details

The encoder already decides which content survives and in what order it renders. Image indices now follow those same merge/sort/drop operations; the renderer does not duplicate those policies or scan text for image markers. The V4.1 renderer applies the order to media and UUIDs together. Existing prompt fixtures and rendering parity checks retain the encoded text.

Duplicate checks covered open PRs, the related Rust PR's changed files and discussion, and V4.1 frontend searches. #56366 changes Rust files only; #60522 only moves Python imports and does not fix this behavior. No matching Python fix was found.

/ci run
✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #95629](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95629) for commit `d8fd027c7f27`.

What this fixes: the assistant calls two tools, `red` then `blue`, and the results come back in the other order, each with an image.

```python
[{"role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [call("red"), call("blue")]},
 {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "blue", "content": [text("blue"), image("blue")]},
 {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "red",  "content": [text("red"),  image("red")]}]
```

The encoder sorts tool results into call order, so the prompt reads `<tool_result>red <image>` then `<tool_result>blue <image>`.

**Broken (main):** images are passed in message order, `[blue, red]`, so each result gets the other result's image.

**Fixed (this PR):** images follow the prompt order, `[red, blue]`.

Verified with `test_tool_images_follow_rendered_order`: it fails on main (`['blue', 'red'] != ['red', 'blue']`) and passes here.

The official DeepSeek encoder had this bug too and fixed it on 2026-10-16 ([`314113f`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6), also in the 1017 release). It now sorts tool results before collecting images, so on the case above it returns `['red.png', 'blue.png']`, the same as this PR.

The approach differs: the reference encoder collects the images itself and returns them in prompt order, while vLLM collects them earlier, so this PR records each image's index and reorders afterwards.
/ci run
✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #95647](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95647) for commit `64b90c287529`.

Thanks @robertgshaw2-redhat for merging main, fixing the test import, validating the regression, and kicking off CI. The explanation and comparison with the official encoder were really helpful. I appreciate your time and help getting this fix reviewed!

`_build_prompt` unpacks `rendered` as `(prompt_raw, image_order)`, and `render_messages_async` now passes `_apply_chat_template_async(...)` directly into `_build_prompt`. Since this PR only updates `_apply_chat_template` to return a tuple, you should ensure `_apply_chat_template_async` also returns the same tuple shape; otherwise async rendering will fail at runtime with an unpacking/type error (and V4.1 may silently skip image reordering in async paths). A concrete fix is to override `_apply_chat_template_async` in these renderers to delegate to the (tuple-returning) `_apply_chat_template` via an executor/`make_async`, so both sync and async share the same contract.

inline_comments.body: `_build_prompt` unpacks `rendered` as `(prompt_raw, image_order)`, and `render_messages_async` now passes `_apply_chat_template_async(...)` directly into `_build_prompt`. Since this PR only updates `_apply_chat_template` to return a tuple, you should ensure `_apply_chat_template_async` also returns the same tuple shape; otherwise async rendering will fail at runtime with an unpacking/type error (and V4.1 may silently skip image reordering in async paths). A concrete fix is to override `_apply_chat_template_async` in these renderers to delegate to the (tuple-returning) `_apply_chat_template` via an executor/`make_async`, so both sync and async share the same contract.

What this fixes: the assistant calls two tools, `red` then `blue`, and the results come back in the other order, each with an image.

```python
[{"role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [call("red"), call("blue")]},
 {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "blue", "content": [text("blue"), image("blue")]},
 {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "red",  "content": [text("red"),  image("red")]}]
```

The encoder sorts tool results into call order, so the prompt reads `<tool_result>red <image>` then `<tool_result>blue <image>`.

**Broken (main):** images are passed in message order, `[blue, red]`, so each result gets the other result's image.

**Fixed (this PR):** images follow the prompt order, `[red, blue]`.

Verified with `test_tool_images_follow_rendered_order`: it fails on main (`['blue', 'red'] != ['red', 'blue']`) and passes here.

The official DeepSeek encoder had this bug too and fixed it on 2026-10-16 ([`314113f`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash/commit/314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6), also in the 1017 release). It now sorts tool results before collecting images, so on the case above it returns `['red.png', 'blue.png']`, the same as this PR.

The approach differs: the reference encoder collects the images itself and returns them in prompt order, while vLLM collects them earlier, so this PR records each image's index and reorders afterwards.

Thanks @robertgshaw2-redhat for merging main, fixing the test import, validating the regression, and kicking off CI. The explanation and comparison with the official encoder were really helpful. I appreciate your time and help getting this fix reviewed!
